newsitem.title: USA: Climber evacuated from McKinley after fall.
newsitem.headline: Climber evacuated from McKinley after fall.

text.p: A climber was evacuated from Alaska's Mount McKinley early Sunday after he fell on his ice axe while travelling on the peak's Muldrow Glacier, the National Park Service said.
Jon Geisen of New York City, a member of a National Outdoor Leadership School expedition, injured his chest in the fall late Saturday night, said Park Service spokesman John Quinley.
The accident occurred at the 12,500-foot level of the 20,320-foot peak, Quinley said.
"He was able to walk, with help from the group, down to their camp at 12,200 feet," Quinley said.
An official at the National Outdoor Leadership School Alaska headquarters, alerted to the accident by cellular telephone, notified the Park Service a few hours later, Quinley said.
The Park Service sent a rescue helicopter to the site early Sunday morning, and Geisen was flown to an Anchorage hospital, Quinley said.
The climber was treated and released, a spokeswoman said.
McKinley, located in Denali National Park, is North America's tallest peak.
